name: value-conversion-v1
idea_origin: Matteo T4; independent drafting from general career reasoning and own manual pilots
hypothesis: A compact responsibility-to-value policy will improve promotion and wealth outcomes by accepting sustainable ownership, securing realistic scope and resources, delivering evidence, and using offered compensation or role negotiations constructively. Unlike growth measured solely by accumulated statistics, it treats useful work and recognition as a conversion chain. This is an untested hypothesis.
change: One newly written Skill. The existing candidate folder was copied for packaging only; its Skill text and policy metadata were replaced. No central candidate instructions, teacher digests or event-answer mappings were used as source text.
predicted_behaviour: When healthy and without urgent warnings, the actor accepts more feasible ownership and cross-team influence opportunities than a defensive baseline. When offered, it clarifies workload/resources and pay-review terms, follows through, and communicates factual contributions. Quarterly choices respond to feedback gaps. Notes remain brief. Promotion timing, final level, wealth, survival, score and tokens are recorded for the frozen actor.
refutation: Do not advance the candidate if actor-matched fresh complete episodes fail to improve level or wealth relative to the current central incumbent under the frozen evaluation protocol, or if any score improvement is outweighed by worse survival or risk outcomes. If the actor does not execute the proposed scope/evidence/negotiation behaviours when offered, classify the mechanism as untested rather than concluding it works. The two historical manual runs are not comparative evidence for this candidate.
notes: Unrun proposal. Baseline is selected by the cloud under the existing protocol; no local games or registry mutation. Same actor and configuration required for comparison. Prior conversation exposed broad central research conclusions and template metadata, so this is independently authored but not a blind outside-model condition. No hidden numerical thresholds, calendar plan, named events or target scores are included in the Skill.
